transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (CTO - Caldera), Janelle Park (Head of Platform), Omar Rahman (NetEng), Liu Chen (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete):
Caldera is evaluating Redwood private deployment for latency-sensitive model inference. Primary asks: private endpoints vs transit gateway for multi-account VPCs, regional gating (APAC restriction), fixed egress IPs for allowlisting partners, and KMS/HSM integration for keys. They want an onramp plan with timeline and a network checklist.

Topics: private onramp, transit gateway vs privatelink, egress IPs/allowlist, multi-region constraints, SOC2/KMS, pricing tiers (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex, AE on the account, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Miguel Torres: Doing well, thanks. We uh we pulled in the right people for network and security cause this is, you know, the main blocker for us.
[00:12] Janelle Park: Yeah, timeline wise we're hoping to have an onramp plan in the next two weeks if possible. We're targetting a pilot in June.
[00:18] Alex Morgan: Great, that's tight but doable. Priya, want to give a quick-redwood overview and then we can jump into Caldera specifics?
[00:25] Priya Sharma: Sure. Quick context — Redwood supports three modes, hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private/VPC deployments. For private we can run a customer-controlled control plane with private endpoints or we can do a transit gateway peering model depending on the customer's networking constraints. There are tradeoffs: private endpoints (Privatelink style) give per-account endpoint isolation and simpler egress control, transit gateway is useful if you have heavy cross-account routing and want fewer endpoints but you may need extra routing and NAT considerations.
[00:52] Omar Rahman: Sorry to interrupt, couple quick items: Our infra is multi-account across three AWS orgs, and we use a central transit gw today for interaccount traffic. We also use egress NAT through a set of bastion NAT instances with fixed elastic IPs that partners expect to see. We need to ensure Redwood traffic can exit through those same fixed IPs for partner allowlists.
[01:12] Priya Sharma: Understood. We have two common patterns for that — 1) use private endpoints in each account that talk to a central proxy in your VPC where egress goes through your NAT, or 2) if you prefer transit-gw peering we can peer into your transit and route outbound through your existing NAT egress. The latter sometimes requires pushing route tables and we coordinate with your network team.
[01:33] Liu Chen: From security we care about KMS integration. Our policy: customer-managed keys only for model logs and any persisted data. Does Redwood support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for private?
[01:43] Priya Sharma: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for disk-level encryption and for audit logs. There's a short one-pager I'll share. There are gotchas around key rotation windows and the onboarding process takes a bit longer than hosted.
[01:57] Alex Morgan: Also want to flag that Dedicated capacity has different SLA and shared-control-plane assumptions vs Private. If you need full VPC isolation and BYOK, Private is usually the lane.
[02:06] Miguel Torres: We're leaning Private because of data residency for APAC and regulatory rules — we can't have model requests egress to non-approved regions. How do you handle region gating?
[02:14] Priya Sharma: We can pin deployments to specific regions and configure routing policies. For Private, the cluster is provisioned in a region you choose; traffic remains in region unless you explicitly route it cross-region. If you need multi-region, we typically propose regional mirrors or a primary-plus-fallback with strict egress controls.
[02:31] Janelle Park: For compliance we'll need proof that the control plane won't route logs through the US if the cluster is in Singapore. Is that documented?
[02:36] Alex Morgan: We have a compliance doc and an architectural diagram that shows control plane endpoints and which metadata is replicated. We'll share that; it's in the security pack. I'll send the link after the call.
[02:47] Omar Rahman: On networking specifics — what about TLS termination? Do we terminate at Redwood endpoints or can we keep mTLS to our ingress?
[02:55] Priya Sharma: We support mutual TLS between your proxy and our workers in Private deployments. Typically you run a small egress proxy or sidecar in your VPC and we mesh with mTLS. There's a cert handshake step during onboarding.
[03:07] Miguel Torres: Ok. A couple of other constraints — we have strict outbound IP allowlists for third-party data providers. We can't add a large ephemeral range; must be fixed set of IPs. How many egress IPs does Redwood need?
[03:18] Priya Sharma: If you want to funnel through your NAT, then you control the outbound IPs. If we host egress from our side (less common for Private) we can allocate static egress IPs but that'll be part of the dedicated/private pricing and needs a configuration for egress pools.
[03:33] Liu Chen: We also need audit logs to be pushed to our SIEM, ideally over a private endpoint or S3 bucket with VPC endpoint. Can Redwood forward logs?
[03:41] Priya Sharma: Yes, Private lets you ship logs to S3 over a VPC endpoint and we can integrate with your SIEM. We also support streaming audit records to your Kafka or PubSub via private peering, but that has additional setup complexity.
[03:55] Alex Morgan: Quick qualification — what's the expected qps/tps for your inference workloads and token rates? That helps size the onramp.
[04:03] Miguel Torres: For the pilot, it's modest — maybe 60 rps peak, 200k tokens per day. But production could be much larger, like 2k rps. So we need to make sure the design can scale.
[04:15] Priya Sharma: Good to know. For that range, private nodes in the region with autoscaling policies should handle it. We might suggest a small reserved pool for predictable latency during pilot then scale into dedicated later.
[04:27] Janelle Park: Any visible cost delta between using private endpoints vs peering through transit? We're trying to estimate networking egress and data transfer costs.
[04:35] Priya Sharma: Network egress costs vary by path: if traffic stays within the same region and uses your NAT, data transfer is typically within AWS free tiers or lower. If we peer across regions, cross-region data transfer costs apply. Private endpoints have minor endpoint-hour costs. We'll put numbers in the checklist we send.
[04:49] Omar Rahman: A nit — in our security baselines we require IP address allocation plan for public facing endpoints (we try to avoid them). Can Redwood run entirely inside our VPC with no public IPs?
[04:59] Priya Sharma: Yes, Private can run without public IPs; control-plane connectivity is via private link to your VPC or a private control plane deployed in your network. There is an option for a relay if you are air-gapped but that requires extra setup.
[05:12] Miguel Torres: There's also a potential legal requirement to have model logs retained for 1 year within Singapore. Can you keep logs in region and ensure deletion policies?
[05:20] Priya Sharma: We can configure S3 buckets in-region with lifecycle policies and we will not replicate logs cross-region unless you request it. We'll call this out in the data residency docs.
[05:29] Alex Morgan: Let's go through a rough onramp checklist live — Priya, maybe run through the networking bullets?
[05:34] Priya Sharma: Sure. Items we usually collect: VPC IDs and account IDs, subnet CIDRs for worker placement, NAT/egress IPs for allowlisting, transit gw config if you want peering, route table ownership for pushing routes, KMS key ARNs, SSO/SAML IDP details for RBAC, and any compliance docs (SOC2/ISO). Also if you want mTLS we need cert exchange info.
[05:56] Janelle Park: We can pull the VPC list and NAT IPs — Omar will send. For SSO we use Okta.
[06:02] Omar Rahman: Yes, I'll send the VPC/route table snapshot and the transit gateway attachments. One question — if we use transit gw peering, do you require route propagation on our side? We're cautious about automatic route pushes.
[06:15] Priya Sharma: We try to avoid pushing routes automatically. Our preference is a manual route they add on your side or a manifest you approve. For larger accounts we do a cross-account CloudFormation that you review.
[06:27] Liu Chen: About SAML — we need role scoping in addition to SSO groups. Does Redwood map groups to roles?
[06:33] Alex Morgan: Yes, we can map SAML groups to Redwood RBAC roles. We'll provide an Okta integration guide.
[06:38] Miguel Torres: Another question — can we do a canary deployment to a single AZ first or do you require multi-AZ? For pilot we may prefer single AZ to reduce blast radius.
[06:48] Priya Sharma: We recommend multi-AZ for production for resiliency, but for initial pilot we can provision single-AZ nodes in a customer VPC, noting the availability risks. We'll document the tradeoffs.
[06:58] Janelle Park: On SLA and fallbacks — if your private cluster hits capacity, can we fail over to dedicated or hosted temporarily?
[07:06] Priya Sharma: Yes, we have routing policies to fallback to a compatible model in another tier; that needs to be part of the rollout decision. If you want strict data residency we can configure fallbacks only within approved regions.
[07:18] Omar Rahman: Ok curious detail — in the transit model do your workers need to be reachable from our subnet ranges or do they originate connections?
[07:25] Priya Sharma: In general, our workers establish outbound connections to your private endpoints — so your VPC needs to accept inbound connections on the privatelink endpoint. If peering into transit gw, route tables must point traffic to that peer. It's a mix; we'll diagram both.
[07:39] Miguel Torres: Can you share a sample network diagram that matches both patterns? It's easier for our infra folks to review.
[07:45] Alex Morgan: Yep, we'll attach two diagrams in the follow-up email — privatelink per-account pattern and transit-gw central pattern.
[07:52] Liu Chen: Small ask — we require mutual TLS for control plane auth and customer-managed KMS for at-rest. Are there any limitations with model KV cache persistence or token caches?
[08:01] Priya Sharma: The KV cache is ephemeral and stays in-region on the worker nodes. We don't persist token content to durable storage unless you opt into a logging pipeline; we can also encrypt in transit and at rest with your keys.
[08:12] Miguel Torres: One more: partners want a consistent egress IP from our VPC. If Redwood endpoints are in our VPC and egress flows through our NAT, we should be good, right?
[08:21] Priya Sharma: Correct — if all egress goes via your NAT, you control the IPs. We'll validate flows during the network deep-dive.
[08:28] Alex Morgan: Let's capture concrete next steps so everyone has clarity. I'll list them and we can adjust. Priya to produce the network checklist and sample diagrams; Omar to send VPC CIDRs and transit gw info; Alex to send security pack and SOC2/KMS one-pager; schedule a technical deep-dive next Tuesday with Omar and Priya.
[08:44] Janelle Park: Sounds good. Can we also get an estimate for incremental cost for static egress IPs if Redwood needs to provide them?
[08:51] Alex Morgan: Yes, we'll include cost estimates in the follow-up — depending on whether you host egress or we allocate egress IPs there are different charges.
[08:59] Miguel Torres: Ok thanks. Quick note — we also evaluate Anthropic and OpenAI — one worry is latency, another is cost. We want to measure p95 latency inside Singapore for a small suite of prompts. Would Redwood run a small benchmark?
[09:11] Priya Sharma: Absolutely. We can spin up a pilot cluster in SG and run p95 measurements against your prompt set. We'll need sample prompts and expected concurrency. That's part of the next step.
[09:22] Omar Rahman: For the benchmark, we want to test with both privatelink and transit setups to compare.
[09:28] Priya Sharma: Good call. We'll capture both.
[09:30] Alex Morgan: Anything else from Caldera?
[09:33] Janelle Park: Not from me. Timeline: we'll try to get the VPC docs by end of week.
[09:37] Miguel Torres: Same. We'll target internal review tomorrow.
[09:40] Alex Morgan: Great — we'll follow up with the checklist, diagrams, SOC2 pack, and a proposed SOW for a pilot. Thanks everyone for your time.
[09:47] (Meeting ends)

Recap (auto):

- Action items captured above.
